meta.finalPromptText: Based on the spec and code you have read, explain how row-level deletes work: position deletes, equality deletes and deletion vectors. Which format versions support each, when does a reader apply them, and what does compaction do with them? Cite the spec sections and the code.
meta.finalAssistantVisibleText:
I've read the relevant spec sections (`Format Versioning`, `Row-level Deletes`, `Scan Planning`, `Delete Formats`, `Appendix E`) and the code that implements them (`DeleteFileIndex.java`, `BaseRewriteFiles.java`, `RewriteFileGroup.java`, plus the rewrite planner classes). Here's the full picture.

## 1. What each delete mechanism is (and which format versions support it)

The spec's versioning and delete-format sections nail this down:

- **V1** — no row-level deletes at all. "Version 1: Analytic Data Tables" (spec:33-38); "Row-level deletes are added by v2 and are not supported in v1" (spec:1356).
- **V2** — adds **position delete files** and **equality delete files** ("Version 2: Row-level Deletes", spec:39-44). `content` field distinguishes `0=data, 1=position deletes, 2=equality deletes`, and `equality_ids` is added for equality deletes (Appendix E, v2 manifest `data_file` changes, spec:~2038-2044).
- **V3** — adds **deletion vectors** (Puffin `deletion-vector-v1` bitmaps, spec:47-57 and spec:1375-1390). Position delete files become **prohibited**: "Position delete files must not be added to v3 tables, but existing position delete files are valid" (spec:1358-1359; enforced in v3 Appendix E: "Writers are not allowed to add new position delete files to v3 tables"). New fields `referenced_data_file`, `content_offset`, `content_size_in_bytes` track DVs (spec:1378-1383, 1947-1951).
- **V4** — writing equality deletes is **prohibited**: "Equality delete files must not be added to v4 tables... Readers must continue to apply equality deletes for v2 and v3 tables and for equality deletes carried over into upgraded v4 tables" (spec:1911-1916).

So:
| Mechanism | v1 | v2 | v3 | v4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Position *delete files* | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ (legacy files still read) | ✗ (legacy still read) |
| Equality delete files | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ (legacy still read) |
| Deletion vectors | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |

- **Position deletes** mark `(file_path, pos)` pairs; the file is sorted by `file_path` then `pos` (spec:1402-1417).
- **Equality deletes** mark rows by column values; delete columns are `equality_ids`, and matching is "all delete columns equal" — a `null` delete value matches `IS NULL` (spec:1418-1470).
- **DVs** are a bitmap per single data file: "A set bit at position P indicates that the row at position P is deleted" (spec:1378-1379). Crucially: "At most one deletion vector is allowed per data file in a snapshot... if a DV is written for a data file, it must replace all previously written position delete files so that when a DV is present, readers can safely ignore matching position delete files" (spec:1386-1390).

The versioning overview also ties it together: position deletes are "encoded in a position delete file (V2) or deletion vector (V3 or above)"; equality deletes "may be created in v2 and v3 tables only" (spec:110-113).

## 2. When a reader applies a delete file to a data file

The authoritative scope rules are in **Scan Planning** (spec:1053-1099). The general principle first: "In general, deletes are applied only to data files that are older and in the same partition" (spec:1088-1089). Then the precise rules:

- **Deletion vector** applies iff: data file's `file_path` == DV's `referenced_data_file`; data file's sequence number **≤** the DV's sequence number; partitions equal (spec:1074-1078).
- **Position delete file** applies iff: `file_path` matches `referenced_data_file` if non-null; data file seq **≤** delete file seq; partitions equal; **and there is no DV that must be applied** (spec:1079-1085) — exactly the "readers can safely ignore matching position delete files" rule.
- **Equality delete file** applies iff: data file seq is **strictly less than** the delete's seq; partitions equal **or** the delete file is unpartitioned (global) (spec:1086-1090, special cases at 1090-1099).

Two important subtleties spelled out:

- Equality deletes with an unpartitioned spec are *global* deletes (spec:1090-1091).
- Position deletes (files and vectors) apply even to data files **from the same commit**, "when the data and delete file data sequence numbers are equal. This allows deleting rows that were added in the same commit" (spec:1091-1099); equality deletes, by contrast, never apply to the same commit (strict `<`).

Readers also *skip* delete work: scan predicates are converted to partition predicates (inclusive projection) that select both data and delete files (spec:1063-1069), and "scan predicates are also used to filter data and delete files using column bounds and counts... If metrics show that a delete file has no rows that match a scan predicate, it may be ignored" (spec:1085-1093).

### Code side: `DeleteFileIndex`

This is the implementation of exactly those rules:

- **Building** — `DeleteFileIndex.builderFor(...)` loads all live delete files for the scan; `build()` (DeleteFileIndex.java:530) sorts them by content: position deletes go by referenced data-file path or by partition (`add`, DeleteFileIndex.java:578-594), equality deletes by partition or into the global bucket for unpartitioned (`add`, DeleteFileIndex.java:596-614), DVs into a dedicated path-keyed map with at most one per file (`add`, DeleteFileIndex.java:568-576; "Can't index multiple DVs" ValidationException at 573-574).
- **Loading** — delete manifest reading is pruned up front: `deleteManifestReaders` (DeleteFileIndex.java:616-659) evaluates a partition-filter of the scan (`evalCache.get(specId).eval(manifest)`, DeleteFileIndex.java:650-652) so whole delete manifests are skipped when stats rule them out.
- **Lookup** — `forDataFile(sequenceNumber, file)` (DeleteFileIndex.java:158-175) calls the four finders. Note the DV priority at 163-170: when a DV is found, the result is `concat(global, eqPartition, dv)` and the *position-delete* lookups are skipped — the code encoding of the spec's "there is no DV that must be applied" rule.
- **Sequence cutoff** — `findStartIndex` (DeleteFileIndex.java:687-703) binary-searches the sorted sequence arrays; only delete files with seq ≥ the data file's seq are candidates. `PositionDeletes.filter` (726-743) applies it for position deletes; `EqualityDeletes.filter` (808-827) adds per-file stats pruning via `canContainEqDeletesForFile` (258). Equality files are indexed by `dataSequenceNumber - 1` (`applySequenceNumber`, DeleteFileIndex.java:879-881) — that minus-1 is the code for the *strictly less than* rule.
- **Stats pruning** — `canContainEqDeletesForFile` (DeleteFileIndex.java:258-323) uses null counts and value bounds (null-overlap logic at 279-292, range overlap via `rangesOverlap` at 326-339) to drop equality delete files that can't possibly match the data file, mirroring spec:1085-1093.

The reader then attaches these to per-file scan tasks; at row-decoding time position deletes/DVs filter by position, equality deletes by probing the delete columns against each row.

## 3. What compaction does with them

Two distinct things, both visible in the code:

**a) Data-file compaction (RewritingDataFiles / bin-pack) folds deletes in and drops them.** The compacted output is written by *applying* the delete files to the input data files (the scan that reads them carries the deletes found by `DeleteFileIndex`), producing new data files with only live rows. The commit then:
- removes the rewritten data files **and** their delete files, and adds the new compacted data files — `BaseRewriteFiles.rewriteFiles(dataFilesToReplace, deleteFilesToReplace, dataFilesToAdd, deleteFilesToAdd)` (BaseRewriteFiles.java:92-127, `deleteFile(DeleteFile)` at 55, `addFile(DeleteFile,...)` at 67-73).
- drops DVs that pointed at rewritten files: `RewriteFileGroup.danglingDVs()` (RewriteFileGroup.java:65-69) collects the DVs of rewritten tasks so they're counted and removed (`removedDeleteFilesCount`, RewriteFileGroup.java:82).

So after compaction, the surviving files reference the same rows with no delete files needed. This is exactly the "replace" operation category: "`replace` -- Data and delete files were added and removed without changing table data; i.e., compaction..." (spec:972).

**b) Safety validation.** Because a compacted file only contains the rows that survived, a concurrent delete for a rewritten file would be lost. Two guards:
- `validateReplacedAndAddedFiles` (BaseRewriteFiles.java:125-138) rejects rewrites that would add files without replacing any.
- `validateNoNewDeletesForDataFiles` (BaseRewriteFiles.java:140) — "if there are replaced data files, there cannot be any new row-level deletes for those data files" — fails the commit if any delete landed against a file being compacted, so the operation retries on the new state instead of silently dropping the delete. This matches the spec's replace-commit requirement: "Replace operations must verify that the files that will be deleted are still in the table... compactions (several files are replaced with a single file that contains the same rows)" (spec:1317).

**c) Positioning for v3/v4.** The spec also mandates how rewrites must preserve the DV invariant: when a DV is created for a data file it must subsume existing position deletes (`spec:1386-1390`, and v3 Appendix E: "These position delete files must be merged into the DV for a data file when one is created"; "Position delete files that contain deletes for more than one data file need to be kept in table metadata until all deletes are replaced by DVs", spec:~1958-1963). There's a dedicated `RewritePositionDeleteFiles` action (`BinPackRewritePositionDeletePlanner`, `RewritePositionDeletesGroup`, etc.) that merges and converts position deletes to DVs for v3+ tables.

## Summary

- **Position deletes** (v2 files, v3+ legacy/DVs): keyed by path+position, applied to data files with seq `<=` delete seq in the same partition, including same-commit rows; skipped entirely if a DV exists for that file (spec:1074-1085; code: DeleteFileIndex.java:163-170).
- **Equality deletes** (v2, v3): keyed by column values, applied to data files with seq **strictly** `<` delete seq, same partition unless unpartitioned/global (spec:1086-1099; code: DeleteFileIndex.java:808-827, applySequenceNumber-1 at 879-881).
- **Deletion vectors** (v3+): single bitmaps per data file, applied on exact path match and seq `<=` (spec:1375-1390; code: DeleteFileIndex.java:217-232).
- **Compaction** applies the deletes while rewriting, then physically drops the delete files/DVs it consumed, guarded by a no-new-deletes validation (BaseRewriteFiles.java:92-140; RewriteFileGroup.java:65-82; spec:972, 1317).

- **Position delete file** applies iff: `file_path` matches `referenced_data_file` if non-null; data file seq **≤** delete file seq; partitions equal; **and there is no DV that must be applied** (spec:1079-1085) — exactly the "readers can safely ignore matching position delete files" rule.
- **Equality delete file** applies iff: data file seq is **strictly less than** the delete's seq; partitions equal **or** the delete file is unpartitioned (global) (spec:1086-1090, special cases at 1090-1099).

Two important subtleties spelled out:

- Equality deletes with an unpartitioned spec are *global* deletes (spec:1090-1091).
- Position deletes (files and vectors) apply even to data files **from the same commit**, "when the data and delete file data sequence numbers are equal. This allows deleting rows that were added in the same commit" (spec:1091-1099); equality deletes, by contrast, never apply to the same commit (strict `<`).

Readers also *skip* delete work: scan predicates are converted to partition predicates (inclusive projection) that select both data and delete files (spec:1063-1069), and "scan predicates are also used to filter data and delete files using column bounds and counts... If metrics show that a delete file has no rows that match a scan predicate, it may be ignored" (spec:1085-1093).

### Code side: `DeleteFileIndex`

This is the implementation of exactly those rules:

- **Building** — `DeleteFileIndex.builderFor(...)` loads all live delete files for the scan; `build()` (DeleteFileIndex.java:530) sorts them by content: position deletes go by referenced data-file path or by partition (`add`, DeleteFileIndex.java:578-594), equality deletes by partition or into the global bucket for unpartitioned (`add`, DeleteFileIndex.java:596-614), DVs into a dedicated path-keyed map with at most one per file (`add`, DeleteFileIndex.java:568-576; "Can't index multiple DVs" ValidationException at 573-574).
- **Loading** — delete manifest reading is pruned up front: `deleteManifestReaders` (DeleteFileIndex.java:616-659) evaluates a partition-filter of the scan (`evalCache.get(specId).eval(manifest)`, DeleteFileIndex.java:650-652) so whole delete manifests are skipped when stats rule them out.
- **Lookup** — `forDataFile(sequenceNumber, file)` (DeleteFileIndex.java:158-175) calls the four finders. Note the DV priority at 163-170: when a DV is found, the result is `concat(global, eqPartition, dv)` and the *position-delete* lookups are skipped — the code encoding of the spec's "there is no DV that must be applied" rule.
- **Sequence cutoff** — `findStartIndex` (DeleteFileIndex.java:687-703) binary-searches the sorted sequence arrays; only delete files with seq ≥ the data file's seq are candidates. `PositionDeletes.filter` (726-743) applies it for position deletes; `EqualityDeletes.filter` (808-827) adds per-file stats pruning via `canContainEqDeletesForFile` (258). Equality files are indexed by `dataSequenceNumber - 1` (`applySequenceNumber`, DeleteFileIndex.java:879-881) — that minus-1 is the code for the *strictly less than* rule.
- **Stats pruning** — `canContainEqDeletesForFile` (DeleteFileIndex.java:258-323) uses null counts and value bounds (null-overlap logic at 279-292, range overlap via `rangesOverlap` at 326-339) to drop equality delete files that can't possibly match the data file, mirroring spec:1085-1093.

The reader then attaches these to per-file scan tasks; at row-decoding time position deletes/DVs filter by position, equality deletes by probing the delete columns against each row.

## 3. What compaction does with them

Two distinct things, both visible in the code:

**a) Data-file compaction (RewritingDataFiles / bin-pack) folds deletes in and drops them.** The compacted output is written by *applying* the delete files to the input data files (the scan that reads them carries the deletes found by `DeleteFileIndex`), producing new data files with only live rows. The commit then:
- removes the rewritten data files **and** their delete files, and adds the new compacted data files — `BaseRewriteFiles.rewriteFiles(dataFilesToReplace, deleteFilesToReplace, dataFilesToAdd, deleteFilesToAdd)` (BaseRewriteFiles.java:92-127, `deleteFile(DeleteFile)` at 55, `addFile(DeleteFile,...)` at 67-73).
- drops DVs that pointed at rewritten files: `RewriteFileGroup.danglingDVs()` (RewriteFileGroup.java:65-69) collects the DVs of rewritten tasks so they're counted and removed (`removedDeleteFilesCount`, RewriteFileGroup.java:82).

So after compaction, the surviving files reference the same rows with no delete files needed. This is exactly the "replace" operation category: "`replace` -- Data and delete files were added and removed without changing table data; i.e., compaction..." (spec:972).

**b) Safety validation.** Because a compacted file only contains the rows that survived, a concurrent delete for a rewritten file would be lost. Two guards:
- `validateReplacedAndAddedFiles` (BaseRewriteFiles.java:125-138) rejects rewrites that would add files without replacing any.
- `validateNoNewDeletesForDataFiles` (BaseRewriteFiles.java:140) — "if there are replaced data files, there cannot be any new row-level deletes for those data files" — fails the commit if any delete landed against a file being compacted, so the operation retries on the new state instead of silently dropping the delete. This matches the spec's replace-commit requirement: "Replace operations must verify that the files that will be deleted are still in the table... compactions (several files are replaced with a single file that contains the same rows)" (spec:1317).

**c) Positioning for v3/v4.** The spec also mandates how rewrites must preserve the DV invariant: when a DV is created for a data file it must subsume existing position deletes (`spec:1386-1390`, and v3 Appendix E: "These position delete files must be merged into the DV for a data file when one is created"; "Position delete files that contain deletes for more than one data file need to be kept in table metadata until all deletes are replaced by DVs", spec:~1958-1963). There's a dedicated `RewritePositionDeleteFiles` action (`BinPackRewritePositionDeletePlanner`, `RewritePositionDeletesGroup`, etc.) that merges and converts position deletes to DVs for v3+ tables.

## Summary

- **Position deletes** (v2 files, v3+ legacy/DVs): keyed by path+position, applied to data files with seq `<=` delete seq in the same partition, including same-commit rows; skipped entirely if a DV exists for that file (spec:1074-1085; code: DeleteFileIndex.java:163-170).
- **Equality deletes** (v2, v3): keyed by column values, applied to data files with seq **strictly** `<` delete seq, same partition unless unpartitioned/global (spec:1086-1099; code: DeleteFileIndex.java:808-827, applySequenceNumber-1 at 879-881).
- **Deletion vectors** (v3+): single bitmaps per data file, applied on exact path match and seq `<=` (spec:1375-1390; code: DeleteFileIndex.java:217-232).
- **Compaction** applies the deletes while rewriting, then physically drops the delete files/DVs it consumed, guarded by a no-new-deletes validation (BaseRewriteFiles.java:92-140; RewriteFileGroup.java:65-82; spec:972, 1317).
